controls.description: Two Rosetta photographs show Šteins during the 2008 approach. The asteroid is only a few dozen pixels wide in each original image, so small surface details aren’t resolved. The grid marks gaps.

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.description: A visualization mosaic compiled by Phil Stooke from Rosetta OSIRIS observations, controlled against Leyrat et al. (2010). Extensive processing, photographed shadows and a revised south-pole interpretation remain; this is not calibrated reflectance. The gray grid marks exterior gaps identified in the published map. Camera detail is approximately 80 m/pixel at best, despite the enlarged map. Shadows adds approximate fixed-epoch Sun lighting.
controls.summary: Photographed shadows, seams and processing edits remain in the published mosaic. The gray grid marks missing map coverage.
controls.title: OSIRIS image mosaic

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: Color shows radius in the published Jorda shape minus a 2.58 km reference sphere. It includes the broad irregular form and is not gravitational elevation. OSIRIS constrains the observed terrain; light-curve inversion supplies the unseen region. The source has a documented artificial elevation jump where those methods meet, retained here. Brightness adds cartographic relief; Shadows adds approximate fixed-epoch Sun lighting.
controls.summary: Height relative to a 2.58 km sphere. The far side is modeled; a source seam joins it to image-based terrain.
controls.title: Shape-derived radial height
